Title: Opening Speech at the Seminar "Impact of Remittances on the Development of Latin America and El Salvador"
CentralBank: Banco Central de Reserva De El Salvador
text: Opening speech of the seminar "Impact of Remittances on the Development of Latin America and El Salvador Lic. Luz Maria de Portillo1 I am pleased to address you this morning, on the occasion of this important event in which the main results of the study "Cerca de Casa: the impact of remittances on the development of Latin America" will be announced. prepared by the World Bank, whom we congratulate on this initiative, which will undoubtedly contribute to a better understanding of migration and remittances. This issue is of great importance for the Central American region, since most countries are net recipients of family remittances, flows that have resulted in a series of transformations at the economic and social level. Remittances are a fundamental part of the economic and social life of El Salvador, representing more than 17% of the Gross Domestic Product (GDP), and about 81% of the Trade Balance of Goods. For those who receive them, they represent a very important average monthly income, they are a relevant source for the financing of local development projects and have become a potential banking tool for external funding through the issuance of securities whose payment flows have been based on remittances. When indicators are observed by country departments, it can be seen that, at the local level, the impact of remittances is much stronger. In three departments, La Union, Morazan and Chalatenango, more than 40% of households are recipients of remittances, reaching its maximum expression in La Union, where half of households receive help from relatives abroad. Year after year, Salvadorans living abroad send significant flows of family remittances that have been distributed to 25% of Salvadoran households that are recipients of remittances, according to the Household Surveys. Undoubtedly, this aid has strengthened the capacity of Salvadoran families to provide education for their children, to have access to health services and for the acquisition of fixed assets, all of which contribute to the social welfare and economic growth of our country. Knowledge of remittances allows us to develop accurate analyses of the impacts on the main macroeconomic and social variables. In this way, it places us in a strategic position for the design of public policy proposals that promote savings and investment. We believe that the best way to do this is to create the macroeconomic and institutional conditions that make the return on investment attractive and sustainable for families receiving remittances. The World Bank study has the merit of opening the debate based on the results that measure the comparative impact of remittances on certain variables in different countries. We already knew about other studies on the subject but now we have the advantage of knowing the details that make the difference to understand the relationship that remittances have with poverty, human capital, the real exchange rate, the cushioning of external shocks and, particularly, financial development. In this sense, the results of the study are incorporated into the country's body of knowledge of this phenomenon, which has become a transversal axis of the country's economic life. Congratulations to the authors of this study. In this same line of investigation, the Central Bank has made contributions 1/ President of the Central Reserve Bank. 3 to complement the analyses. This morning we are going to know one of the studies carried out and I want to tell you that we are currently processing the information of the second survey on remittances recently carried out in the main communities where our compatriots work in the United States. The results that we will obtain from this survey are added to those collected internally by other surveys, in order to have a broad picture, not only of the best estimate of the data, the origins and nature of migration, but more importantly, to know from the primary source and directly, the impacts of these flows on macro and microeconomic variables. Know the needs of senders to be able to channel them to productive uses, integrate a service offer to those needs and also know the human face of the flow of remittances. This information will be complemented by the results of the Population and Housing Censuses, the Agricultural Census and the generation of the new system of national accounts that we are developing. There we will see how the economic and social reality of the country has changed, largely as a result of migrations and family remittances. The debate that the World Bank opens with this study forces us to be creative to promote, among other aspects, the development of the financial system. The reality in our country has changed rapidly with recent acquisitions, since we have leading banks operating in El Salvador and taking advantage of the regional scale that local banks had already achieved. The context that El Salvador is dollarized, of having an FTA with the United States, of generating about US 3,500 million annually in family remittance flows and that the country is emerging from the lower part of the economic cycle with growth of more than 4%, implies in the financial system the development of new products and an integrated offer of several financial services. This represents an opportunity to generate better possibilities for channeling and efficient use of family remittance flows. The community of Salvadorans abroad is strong and maintains close ties with the country, not only remittances are generated, but also tourism, exports of nostalgic products, investment in real estate, health services and community aid, among others. The above paints a picture with ample business possibilities for Salvadorans and a field of development for the financial services they demand. Likewise, another great challenge is the achievement of lower shipping costs, which is being promoted by international organizations. Family remittances, more than an economic issue, is a human issue that reflects family ties and values that are not lost, but strengthened by distance. The technical contributions of the World Bank are a contribution to the generation of critical and creative thinking in this task of seeking greater national development. Finally, I urge you to have an active participation in the discussion that motivates the issue of family remittances that is of great importance in Latin America. 4

Luz Mara de Portillo1 Me complace dirigirme a ustedes esta maana, en ocasin de este importante evento en el que se darn a conocer los principales resultados del estudio "Cerca de Casa: el impacto de las remesas en el desarrollo de Amrica Latina", elaborado por el Banco Mundial, a quin felicitamos por esta iniciativa que sin duda contribuir a un mejor entendimiento de las migraciones y de las remesas. Este tema es de gran importancia para la regin centroamericana, ya que la mayora de pases somos receptores netos de remesas familiares, flujos que han dado como resultado una serie de transformaciones a nivel econmico y social. Las remesas son parte fundamental de la vida econmica y social de El Salvador, representan ms del 17% del Producto Interno Bruto (PIB), y cerca del 81% de la Balanza Comercial de Bienes. Para quienes las reciben representan un ingreso promedio mensual muy importante, son una fuente relevante para el financiamiento de proyectos de desarrollo local y se han convertido en una herramienta bancaria potencial de fondeo externo mediante la emisin de valores cuyos flujos de pago se han sustentado en remesas. Cuando se observan indicadores por departamentos del pas, puede observarse que, a nivel local, el impacto de las remesas es mucho ms fuerte. En tres departamentos, La Unin, Morazn y Chalatenango, ms del 40% de los hogares son receptores de remesas, alcanzando su mxima expresin en La Unin, donde la mitad de los hogares reciben ayuda de sus parientes en el exterior. Ao a ao los salvadoreos que residen en el exterior envan importantes flujos de remesas familiares que se han distribuido en 25% de los hogares salvadoreos que son receptores de remesas, de acuerdo a las Encuestas de Hogares. Sin duda, esta ayuda ha fortalecido la capacidad de las familias salvadoreas para brindar educacin a sus hijos, para tener acceso a servicios de salud y para la adquisicin de activos fijos, todo lo cual contribuye al bienestar social y al crecimiento econmico de nuestro pas. El conocimiento de las remesas nos permite desarrollar anlisis certeros sobre los impactos en las principales variables macroeconmicas y sociales. De esa manera, nos coloca en una posicin estratgica para el diseo de propuestas de polticas pblicas que propicien el ahorro y la inversin. Consideramos que la mejor forma de hacerlo es creando las condiciones macroeconmicas e institucionales que vuelvan atractiva y sostenible la rentabilidad de la inversin para las familias receptoras de remesas. El estudio del Banco Mundial tiene el mrito de abrir el debate teniendo como base los resultados que miden el impacto comparativo de las remesas sobre determinadas variables en diferentes pases. Ya conocamos otros estudios sobre el tema pero ahora tenemos la ventaja de conocer los detalles que hacen la diferencia para entender la relacin que tienen las remesas con la pobreza, el capital humano, el tipo de cambio real, el amortiguamiento de los shocks externos y, particularmente, el desarrollo financiero. En ese sentido, los resultados del estudio se incorporan al acervo de conocimientos que el pas tiene de este fenmeno, que se ha convertido en un eje transversal de la vida econmica del pas. Por ello mis felicitaciones a los autores de este estudio. En esa misma lnea de investigacin, el Banco Central ha hecho aportes 1/ Presidenta del Banco Central de Reserva. 3 para complementar los anlisis. Esta maana vamos a conocer uno de los estudios realizados y quiero comentarles que en estos momentos nos encontramos procesando la informacin de la segunda encuesta sobre remesas realizada recientemente en las principales comunidades donde trabajan nuestros compatriotas en Estados Unidos. Los resultados que obtendremos de esa encuesta, se suman a los recabados internamente por otras encuestas, a fin de tener un panorama amplio, no slo de la mejor estimacin del dato, los orgenes y naturaleza de la migracin, sino ms importante an, conocer de la fuente primaria y en forma directa, los impactos de esos flujos en las variables macro y microeconmicas, conocer las necesidades de los remitentes para poder canalizarlas a usos productivos, integrar una oferta de servicios a esas necesidades y conocer tambin el rostro humano del flujo de remesas. Esa informacin se complementar con los resultados de los Censos de Poblacin y Vivienda, el Censo Agropecuario y la generacin del nuevo sistema de cuentas nacionales que estamos desarrollando. Ah veremos cmo la realidad econmica y social del pas ha cambiado, en gran medida producto de las migraciones y las remesas familiares. El debate que abre el Banco Mundial con este estudio nos obliga a ser creativos para propiciar, entre otros aspectos, el desarrollo del sistema financiero. La realidad en nuestro pas ha cambiado aceleradamente con las recientes adquisiciones, ya que tenemos a bancos de primer orden operando en El Salvador y aprovechando la escala regional que ya haban logrado los bancos locales. El contexto de que El Salvador est dolarizado, de tener un TLC con Estados Unidos, de generar cerca de US$ 3,500 millones anuales en flujos de remesas familiares y de que el pas est saliendo de la parte baja del ciclo econmico con crecimientos superiores al 4%, implica en el sistema financiero el desarrollo de nuevos productos y una oferta integrada de varios servicios financieros. Esto representa una oportunidad de generar mejores posibilidades para una canalizacin y uso eficiente de los flujos de remesas familiares. La comunidad de salvadoreos en el exterior es fuerte y mantiene vnculos estrechos con el pas, no solamente se generan remesas, sino tambin turismo, exportaciones de productos nostlgicos, inversin en bienes races, servicios de salud y ayuda comunitaria, entre otros. Lo anterior nos dibuja un panorama con amplias posibilidades de negocios para los salvadoreos y un campo de desarrollo para los servicios financieros que demandan. Asimismo, otro gran reto es el logro de menores costos de envo, que est siendo impulsado por organismos internacionales. Las remesas familiares, ms que un tema econmico, es un tema humano que refleja los vnculos y valores familiares que no se pierden, sino que se fortalecen con la distancia. Los aportes tcnicos del Banco Mundial son una contribucin a la generacin de pensamiento crtico y creativo en esta tarea de bsqueda de mayor desarrollo nacional. Final-mente, los exhorto a tener una participacin activa en la discusin que motiva el tema de las remesas familiares que es de gran trascendencia en Latinoamrica. 4

Title: Speech at Redibacen Conference
CentralBank: Banco Central de Reserva De El Salvador
text: OPENING SPEECH OF REDIBACEN CONFERENCE "ANALYSIS OF FISCAL ADJUSTMENT IN EL SALVADOR BASED ON GROSS NATIONAL DISPOSABLE INCOME (GDI)" WEDNESDAY, MARCH 27, 2019  8:15 A.M. Good morning Licda. Marta Evelyn de Rivera, Vice President of the Central Reserve Bank MSc. Kenny Mendoza  Senior of the Dept. of Financial and Fiscal Statistics MSc. Cesar Alvarado  Senior of the Dept. of Economic and Financial Research of the BCR Mr. Carlos Sanabria  Head of the Department of Economic and Financial Research of the BCR Members of REDIBACEN Friends of the press It is a pleasure to welcome you to a new conference of the Network of Researchers of the Central Bank, where an effort is made to share with you, studies technicians of high relevance to the Salvadoran economy. This day the conference "Analysis of the Fiscal Adjustment in El Salvador from the Gross National Disposable Income" takes place. Other studies conducted at the Central Bank have shown how economic growth is the key to making public debt sustainable, given our structural characteristics, especially our condition as a dollarized economy. This is because, with greater economic growth, incomes increase at a rate that allows the cost of debt to be paid. The deficit of central governments in Latin America in the last decade, as well as the high percentage of public debt, has caused various economic analysts and international organizations to propose fiscal adjustments for the economies of the region in an attempt to balance public finances. However, such measures should be taken with caution. It should be remembered that public spending has a social function of providing important services such as education, health, security, environmental care, among others, which affect the living conditions of all, especially those low-income groups that are direct beneficiaries of the different public care programs. Additionally, public spending has a multiplier effect on the economy, so reducing it would translate into lower economic growth. For example, estimates made by the Central Bank show that, for every dollar of consumer spending made by the Government, between 0.60 and 0.70 of production are generated in the economy in the short term, while, in the long term, that same dollar can generate up to an additional 0.80. On the other hand, fiscal adjustments on the revenue side also represent some risks, especially when the measures are aimed at increasing indirect taxes. El Salvador is a country with a regressive tax system, in which VAT represents a little more than 40% of total revenue. The Central Bank has made estimates of the effects of increasing the VAT, identifying for example that going from the current 13% to 15%, would cause the Salvadoran economy to slow down, registering positive growth rates but lower by about 1.0 to 1.5 percentage points less compared to a situation in which said tax is not modified. On the other hand, the Central American Institute of Fiscal Studies (ICEFI) conducted a study for Guatemala, Honduras and El Salvador evaluating the effect on poverty and inequality of an increase in VAT. In the case of In our country, ICEFI states that increasing VAT from 13% to 15%, household consumption would decrease, increase inequality by 0.0244 points and increase total poverty by 2.42 percentage points. Meanwhile, the International Monetary Fund, in its Article IV of 2018, notes that in El Salvador pension reform and the targeting of subsidies and capital spending have been key factors that have driven an improvement in recent years. However, it has made the recommendation to implement a fiscal adjustment of 2.0% of GDP in 2019-2020 to reduce the public debt ratio to 60% of GDP in 2024, including measures such as increasing the VAT rate to 15%, implementing a property tax and eliminating tax exemptions. The agency claims that growth would only slow 0.75 percentage points and would not be negatively affected thereafter. However, the Central Reserve Bank has stated that the fiscal adjustment in the country must be gradual, to be executed in the medium and long term and thus not affect the growth of the Salvadoran economy, since, due to its structural characteristics, an abrupt and strong adjustment would cause negative consequences. especially because of the absence of monetary policy. On the other hand, it has been emphasized that the IMF uses the Gross Domestic Product for the calculation of the fiscal adjustment for El Salvador, while, from our perspective, the appropriate variable for this analysis is the Gross Disposable National Income. Although GDP is the most well-known and used variable for Analyzing the performance of economies is not the one that best reflects the amount of resources that residents of a country have to spend or allocate to savings. Instead, Gross National Disposable Income indicates a country's actually disposable income to meet its expenditures and savings, as well as express its ability to honor its debt commitments. In El Salvador, the Gross National Disposable Income is strengthened by the flow of family remittances, which in the last three decades has represented between 15% and 20% of GDP, constituting in turn an important source of income for the country, specifically, households. In this morning's conference, speakers will explain the relationship between this type of revenue stream and public finances, an element that is fundamental to be able to reaffirm the need to modify the traditional Debt to GDP ratio to create a more accurate representation of sustainability. of Salvadoran debt, using instead the ratio Debt to Gross Disposable National Income. This is how I invite you to debate on this issue that interests the country and that represents an economic policy decision that must be taken based on concrete estimates and attached to the structural characteristics of the Salvadoran economy, especially because of the effects it would have on the living conditions of the population. Thanks a lot.
text_original: DISCURSO INAUGURACIN DE CONFERENCIA REDIBACEN ANALISIS DEL AJUSTE FISCAL EN EL SALVADOR A PARTIR DEL INGRESO NACIONAL BRUTO DISPONIBLE (INBD) MIRCOLES 27 DE MARZO 2019  8:15 A.M.  Muy buenos das  Licda. Marta Evelyn de Rivera, Vicepresidente del Banco Central de Reserva  MSc. Kenny Mendoza  Senior del Depto. de Estadsticas Financieras y Fiscales  MSc. Csar Alvarado  Senior del Depto. de Investigacin Econmica y Financiera del BCR  Ing. Carlos Sanabria  Jefe del Departamento de Investigacin Econmica y Financiera del BCR  Miembros de REDIBACEN  Amigos de la prensa Es un gusto darles la bienvenida a una nueva conferencia de la Red de Investigadores del Banco Central, donde se realiza un esfuerzo por compartir con ustedes, estudios tcnicos de alta relevancia para la economa salvadorea. Este da se desarrolla la conferencia Anlisis del Ajuste Fiscal en El Salvador a partir del Ingreso Nacional Bruto Disponible. Otros estudios realizados en el Banco Central han demostrado cmo el crecimiento econmico es la clave para hacer sostenible la deuda pblica, dadas nuestras caractersticas estructurales, especialmente nuestra condicin de economa dolarizada. Esto es as porque, con mayor crecimiento econmico, los ingresos incrementan a un ritmo que permite pagar el costo de la deuda. El dficit de los gobiernos centrales en Amrica Latina en la ltima dcada, as como el alto porcentaje de deuda pblica, ha generado que diversos analistas econmicos y organismos internacionales propongan los ajustes fiscales para las economas de la regin en un intento por equilibrar las finanzas pblicas. Sin embargo, este tipo de medidas deben ser tomadas con cautela. Debe recordarse que el gasto pblico tiene una funcin social de proveer servicios importantes como la educacin, salud, seguridad, cuidado del medio ambiente, entre otros, que afectan las condiciones de vida de todos, especialmente de aquellos grupos de bajos ingresos que son beneficiarios directos de los distintos programas de atencin pblica. Adicionalmente el gasto pblico tiene un efecto multiplicador en la economa, por lo que la reduccin del mismo se traducira en un menor crecimiento econmico. Por ejemplo, estimaciones realizadas por el Banco Central muestran que, por cada dlar de gasto de consumo realizado por el Gobierno, se generan entre $0.60 y $0.70 de produccin en la economa en el corto plazo, mientras que, en el largo plazo, ese mismo dlar puede llegar a generar hasta $0.80 adicionales. Por otra parte, ajustes fiscales por el lado de los ingresos pblicos tambin representan algunos riesgos, especialmente cuando las medidas se orientan al incremento de impuestos indirectos. El Salvador es un pas con un sistema tributario regresivo, en el que el IVA representa un poco ms del 40% del total de la recaudacin. El Banco Central ha realizado estimaciones de los efectos de incrementar el IVA, identificndose por ejemplo que pasar del actual 13% a un 15%, provocara que la economa salvadorea se desacelere, registrando tasas de crecimiento positivas pero inferiores en alrededor de 1.0 a 1.5 puntos porcentuales menos en comparacin a una situacin en el que dicho impuesto no se modifique. Por otra parte, el Instituto Centroamericano de Estudios Fiscales (ICEFI) realiz un estudio para Guatemala, Honduras y El Salvador evaluando el efecto en la pobreza y desigualdad de un aumento en el IVA. En el caso de nuestro pas, ICEFI afirma que de aumentar el IVA del 13% al 15%, el consumo de los hogares disminuira, incrementara la desigualdad en 0.0244 puntos y aumentara la pobreza total en 2.42 puntos porcentuales. Mientras tanto, el Fondo Monetario Internacional, en su Artculo IV de 2018, seala que en El Salvador la reforma de pensiones y la focalizacin de los subsidios y el gasto de capital han sido factores clave que han impulsado una mejora en los ltimos aos. Sin embargo, ha realizado la recomendacin de implementar un ajuste fiscal del 2.0% del PIB en 2019-2020 para reducir el ratio de la deuda pblica a 60% del PIB en 2024, incluyendo medidas tales como aumentar la tasa del IVA a 15%, implementar un impuesto a la propiedad y eliminar las exenciones fiscales. El organismo afirma que el crecimiento solo disminuira 0.75 puntos porcentuales y que no se vera afectado negativamente a partir de entonces. No obstante, el Banco Central de Reserva ha manifestado que el ajuste fiscal en el pas debe ser gradual, para ejecutarse en el mediano y largo plazo y as no afectar el crecimiento de la economa salvadorea, ya que, debido a las caractersticas estructurales de la misma, un ajuste abrupto y de fuerte magnitud ocasionara consecuencias negativas, en especial por la ausencia de poltica monetaria. Por otra parte, se ha hecho hincapi en que el FMI utiliza el Producto Interno Bruto para el clculo del ajuste fiscal para El Salvador, mientras que, desde nuestra ptica, la variable apropiada para dicho anlisis es el Ingreso Nacional Bruto Disponible. Aunque el PIB es la variable ms conocida y utilizada para analizar el desempeo de las economas, no es la que mejor refleja la cantidad de recursos con que cuentan los residentes de un pas para gastar o destinar al ahorro. En cambio, el Ingreso Nacional Bruto Disponible indica el ingreso realmente disponible de un pas para realizar sus gastos y ahorro, as como expresar su capacidad para honrar sus compromisos de deuda. En El Salvador, el Ingreso Nacional Bruto Disponible se fortalece por el flujo de remesas familiares, que en las ltimas tres dcadas ha representado entre el 15% y 20% del PIB, constituyendo a su vez una importante fuente de ingresos para el pas, especficamente, los hogares. En la conferencia de esta maana, los expositores nos explicarn la relacin que existe entre este tipo de flujos de ingresos y las finanzas pblicas, un elemento que es fundamental para poder reafirmar la necesidad de modificar la relacin tradicional Deuda sobre PIB para crear una representacin ms precisa de la sostenibilidad de la deuda salvadorea, usando en su lugar, el ratio Deuda sobre Ingreso Nacional Bruto Disponible. Es as como los invito a debatir sobre este tema que interesa al pas y que representa una decisin de poltica econmica que debe ser tomada con base en estimaciones concretas y apegadas a las caractersticas estructurales de la economa salvadorea, sobre todo por los efectos que tendra sobre las condiciones de vida de la poblacin. Muchas gracias.

Title: Speech at the Signing of the Regional Treaty on Payments and Securities Settlement
CentralBank: Banco Central de Reserva De El Salvador
text: Speech for the signing of the Regional Treaty on Payments and Settlement of Securities Laura Ayala de Flores1 Ms. President of the Central Reserve Bank Ms. Vice President of the Central Reserve Bank Mr. Executive Secretary of the Central American Monetary Council Members of the Executive Committee, Strategic Payments Committee, and Technical Committee on Payment Systems Ladies and Gentlemen We are gathered today to witness the signing by the Republic of El Salvador, of the "Treaty on payment and securities settlement systems of Central America and the Dominican Republic" The Treaty is an international legal instrument aimed at providing legal certainty, developing and strengthening systemically important payment and securities settlement systems in the region, and strengthening central banks' powers over payment systems. The Treaty incorporates the most relevant international standards on the subject, adjusting them to the reality and needs of the member countries of the Council, and constitutes an important factor of harmonization, with a view to the development and financial integration of the region. This regulation is the product of a project developed by the CMCA and its Executive Secretariat with the cooperation of the IDB and the active participation of the Central Banks of the region, which aims to harmonize and strengthen the region's payment systems, of special relevance in the current situation of development of financial markets and in the face of new commercial relations between our peoples and governments. Thus, in November 2005, the CMCA, at a meeting held in San Salvador, approved the text of the Treaty. Payment and securities settlement systems are essential to ensure the proper functioning of financial markets and the economy in general. The increase in recent years in the number of transfers and in the total amount traded between financial institutions in the countries of the region, and with the rest of the world, has intensified the need to provide these systems with greater legal certainty and to strengthen the powers of surveillance over them, since their solidity and legal certainty is a fundamental requirement to maintain and promote financial stability. Benefits arising from the Treaty The main benefits derived from this regional regulation are the following: a) It harmonizes and strengthens the systemically important payment systems of the countries of the region, providing adequate protection to the growing local and international operations that are carried out through them, and reinforces their vigilance. Guarantees the legal certainty of the systems that work that exist or come into existence, even in times of crisis of any of the participating banks, avoiding the spread of negative effects; b) promotes the financial integration of the region, through uniform and harmonized regulations, providing foundation and adequate regulation and oversight of systems of a regional nature; c) completes the internal rules of national systems, strengthening their legal and regulatory frameworks and promoting a benchmark for their improvement; d) strengthens the powers of central banks for the oversight of national systems, and those of the CMAQ for the surveillance of regional systems; e) adequately regulates the determination of the applicable regulations when entities of different nationalities participate in a system, a possibility that is increasingly frequent in the region due to the current financial integration; and f) It encourages the supranational and Community treatment that may be given in the future to other areas such as the supervision and supervision of financial systems, the adoption of accounting standards and the consolidated supervision of banks and other financial institutions. The Treaty is an important regulation that meets the highest international standards in this area. It is a significant step in the search for the strengthening and harmonization of the systems of the Region, and its entry into force will allow all our countries to incorporate into their legal system, with a higher rank, a body of norms that, by reflecting the most relevant international standards, will grant sufficient legal certainty to existing systems and those that will be constituted in the future. are national or regional, facilitating their development. It is, in short, a powerful instrument for the financial integration of the region. That is why we are pleased that today the President of the Central Reserve Bank, in her capacity as Plenipotentiary of the Republic of El Salvador, will sign this Regional Treaty. San Salvador, 19 December 2006 1 Head of the Legal Department and Representative of the BCR in the Legal Studies Committee of the CMCA 17
text_original: Discurso por la firma del Tratado Regional de Pagos y Liquidacin de Valores Laura Ayala de Flores1 Sra Presidenta del Banco Central de Reserva Sra Vice Presidenta del Banco Central de Reserva Sr. Secretario Ejecutivo del Consejo Monetario centroamericano Seores miembros del Comit Ejecutivo, Comit Estratgico de Pagos, y Comit Tcnico de Sistemas de Pagos Seores y seoras Estamos este da reunidos para presenciar la suscripcin por parte de la Republica de El Salvador, del "Tratado sobre sistemas de pagos y de liquidacin de valores de Centroamrica y Repblica Dominicana" El Tratado es un instrumento jurdico internacional cuyo objetivo es propiciar la seguridad jurdica, el desarrollo y el fortalecimiento de los sistemas de pagos y de liquidacin de valores con importancia sistmica de la regin, y fortalecer las competencias de los bancos centrales sobre los sistemas de pagos. El Tratado incorpora los estndares internacionales ms relevantes sobre la materia, ajustndolos a la realidad y necesidades de los pases miembros del Consejo, y constituye un importante factor de armonizacin, con vistas en el desarrollo y la integracin financiera de la regin. Esta normativa es producto de proyecto desarrollado por el CMCA y su Secretara Ejecutiva con la cooperacin del BID y la participacin activa de los Bancos Centrales de la regin, que tiene por objeto la armonizacin y fortalecimiento de los sistemas de pagos de la regin, de especial relevancia en la actual coyuntura de desarrollo de los mercados financieros y frente a las nuevas relaciones comerciales entre nuestros pueblos y gobiernos. Es as como en noviembre de 2005, el CMCA en reunin realizada en San Salvador, aprueba el texto del Tratado. Los sistemas de pagos y de liquidacin de valores son esenciales para asegurar el buen funcionamiento de los mercados financieros y de la economa en general.
